name: Natu Kodi Iguru
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker and add curry leaves and chopped onions. Sauté until golden brown.
2. Add the ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies; sauté until the raw smell disappears.
3. Add the country chicken pieces along with turmeric and salt. Sauté on medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes until the meat changes color and releases moisture.
4. Add red chili powder and coriander powder. Mix well and cook covered for 10-15 minutes, adding a little water if necessary.
5. Once the chicken is partially tender, add the poppy seeds paste and cook until the oil begins to separate from the gravy.
6. Sprinkle garam masala, stir thoroughly, and cook until the gravy reaches a thick, coating consistency.
7. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with ragi mudde, rice, or parotta.
description: Natu Kodi Iguru is a quintessential Andhra delicacy made using free-range country chicken. Known for its intense heat and deep, complex flavors, it is a celebratory dish often prepared in rural households. The use of country chicken provides a firm texture and rich taste that pairs perfectly with the spicy, onion-based gravy, reflecting the bold culinary heritage of the Rayalaseema and coastal regions of Andhra Pradesh.
